branches.note: Past-due (delinquent) taxes must be paid with guaranteed funds ONLY: cashier's check, cash, debit card, or credit card. Personal checks are NOT accepted for delinquent taxes per local TCSLC policy (backed by §197.333 — interest and fees accrue on delinquency).

Installment plan application (DR-534) per §197.222 — application must be submitted by April 30 for the upcoming tax year. Four installments due June 30 (6% discount), Sep 30 (4.5%), Dec 31 (3%), Mar 31 (0%). Customer must be the owner to sign.
Partial payment applies to CURRENT-year taxes only (before delinquency), must be made in up to 3 payments by March 31, no tax discounts apply on partial payments, and minimum $100 per payment.

Property tax mailing-address change is a two-step process: first submit the change on the Property Appraiser's form (paslc.gov), then submit on the Tax Collector's form (tcslc.com). Appraiser-side must be completed before the Tax Collector side.
Property tax EXEMPTION applications (homestead, senior, disability, veteran) are filed with the Property Appraiser (paslc.gov), not the Tax Collector. Customer directed there.

Standard current-year payment — personal checks, cash, credit, debit, or cashier's check accepted. Florida discount schedule applies (§197.162): 4% November, 3% December, 2% January, 1% February, 0% March. A government-issued photo ID is required to make an IN-OFFICE payment (so any refund can be issued to the person who paid); online, mail, and third-party payments don't need one. [Confirmed by TCSLC staff — policy-questions TAX-5, 2026-07.]
Customer is not the property owner — installment plan and partial-payment application must be signed by the owner. Standard current-year payment can be made by anyone.
